//: Named subject sets for `sentinel connect sweep <set>`. Edit this file as you learn names — every abatement agreement and utility filing names the actual contracting entity, and that name is the one worth searching. A subject here is a SEARCH STRING, not a claim that the entity is involved in anything.

datacenters.note: Operators and the single-purpose entities they file under.

energy.note: The supply side. AEP Ohio is the distribution utility for central Ohio; PJM runs the interconnection queue that decides whether a load can be served at all.

newalbany.note: Land assembly and the development vehicles.

lobbying.note: Firms already seen carrying more than one side of the question. Add any registrant the graph surfaces.

surveillance.note: Vendors whose products are bought by police departments. A name here is a SEARCH STRING, not a claim that the vendor operates in Ohio.

surveillance_money.note: The funding streams. Federal grant programmes and the Ohio agencies that receive or administer them.

surveillance_platforms.note: Platform companies as ENTITIES. These were written as 'Meta Platforms law enforcement' — an entity glued to a concept — which the phrase fix then sent as one exact quoted string that appears in no document, so the sweep returned nothing and the nothing looked like an answer. A subject must be a NAME. The concept belongs in which register you ask, not in the query.

ratepayers.note: Who pays for the power a data center needs. The tariff fights, the utilities, and the offices that represent customers rather than shareholders.

hb6.note: House Bill 6 and its aftermath. Adjudicated federal corruption, not allegation -- and the reason Ohio ratepayers are already paying for generation decisions made under it.

outside_oh_senate.note: Committees that spent independently at the Ohio Senate seat, cycle 2026. Support and opposition are listed together because the SET is the subject — which committees showed up at all — and separating them here would bake a side into the search. $19.1m moved at this seat against $476k into the candidate's own account: OUTSIDE PRESSURE 40.19x. NOTE: 'The Sentinel Action Fund' is an unrelated national super PAC and has nothing to do with this desk.

outside_oh_house.note: Committees spending independently at Ohio House seats, cycle 2024, and the candidate-adjacent vehicles beside them. A victory fund is the member's own joint committee, not an outside group — it is here to be recognised, not conflated.

single_target_pacs.note: Committees found spending against ONE named member. Concentration is a measured fact and not intent — see `connect asymmetry`. United for Common Sense is here as the counter-example: 94.9% of its money went against a different candidate entirely, so it is NOT single-target and the set exists partly to keep that visible.

conduits.note: Committees that FORWARD other people's earmarked money rather than giving their own. Their Schedule B totals are individuals' donations passing through and must never be reported as the organisation's giving.

persona_management.note: The documented precedent for automated persona operations, and the platforms they run on. HBGARY FEDERAL's 2011 breach put 'persona management' proposals into the public record, and NTREPID held a US CENTCOM contract for online persona management — that one is federal CONTRACTING, so usaspending can speak to it. Everything here is an entity name. NONE of it is evidence that any platform operates a bot farm: platforms publish takedown reports about third-party networks, which is the opposite claim.

intel_newalbany.note: The Licking County semiconductor and data-centre build, by ENTITY NAME. The federal hooks are real and few: CHIPS money is a federal AWARD, so usaspending can speak to it; the companies lobby, so senatelda can; and large-load interconnection is a FERC matter. Everything else about this story — the parcels, the abatements, the tax-increment financing, the water and the tariff — is COUNTY and STATE and appears in no register queried here. An empty federal answer about a land deal is a fact about the register, not about the deal.

bot_economy.note: THE ANSWER TO "do data centres have a connection to bot farms" is: not the one the phrase implies. A hyperscale campus is where ad INVENTORY is manufactured and where fraud is DETECTED — not where the bots live. Datacenter-originated traffic is, by industry definition, the marker used to CLASSIFY traffic as non-human, which is why fraud rings rent cloud capacity and why the platforms publish datacenter IP lists to exclude it. The three groups here are the three sides of that trade and they are not the same: firms PAID TO MEASURE fraud, platforms that SELL the inventory, and vendors that BUILD synthetic personas. None of these names is alleged to operate a bot farm.

message_buyers.note: WHO THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT PAYS TO DISTRIBUTE A MESSAGE. This is not a covert register — it is appropriated money, competed and published, and that is exactly why it is useful: it establishes that algorithmic reach is a line item with a price. The live Google run found U.S. Agency for Global Media paying $803,070 across 24 awards for Google and YouTube advertising for VOA language services (account 113-548-8374 is printed in the contract text), State Department $239,158 to MARKET TO PUBLIC DIPLOMACY PROGRAMS AND PRODUCTS, and FDA $206,454 for GOOGLE ADWORDS CAMPAIGNS tagged IGF::CT::IGF — the contracting officer classifying ad buying as a CRITICAL function. Consensus-building with a federal appropriation behind it, bought through the same auction as everything else.

election_record.note: THE ADJUDICATED RECORD OF THE 2020 ELECTION CLAIMS. This set exists because "election fraud" is the exact shape of query that returns confident wrong answers — the Zhukov/Methbot/Devumi run got 3 of 4 wrong. The fix is to stop searching for a conclusion and start reading DOCKETS. These are the parties to litigation that actually produced findings of fact. A court ruling on falsity is evidence of a different and much stronger kind than a news report, because it survived discovery and cross-examination. DENOMINATOR RULE APPLIES HARDEST HERE: documented individual voter-fraud prosecutions do exist, and a count of them means nothing without the number of ballots cast beside it.

platform_moderation.note: THE LAPTOP AND THE THROTTLING, AS LITIGATION AND AS PRIMARY DOCUMENTS. Three separate questions that get told as one story: (1) are the emails genuine, (2) did platforms suppress the story, (3) did government cause them to. Each has a different register and a different answer, and conflating them is how both sides of this argument go wrong. The federal prosecution is where laptop-derived evidence was actually litigated; Murthy v. Missouri is where the jawboning question was actually decided, and it was decided on STANDING, which is the most misreported fact in the whole affair.

minnesota_fraud.note: FEEDING OUR FUTURE AND THE MINNESOTA PROGRAM PROSECUTIONS. The fraud here is REAL, CHARGED AND IN LARGE PART CONVICTED — the largest pandemic-relief prosecution in the country, roughly 70 defendants in D. Minn., and a juror in the first trial was offered a bag of cash. None of that is in dispute and none of it needs a viral video to establish it. What a viral video adds is a FRAME, and the frame is the part to check separately: a federal indictment names defendants, amounts and programs, and it does not name a community. Read the docket for what was charged; read the Legislative Auditor for what oversight failed; treat any claim that outruns both as a claim.

foreign_lobby.note: WHO IS PAID TO REPRESENT A FOREIGN GOVERNMENT IN WASHINGTON. Read the register boundary before reading a result. FARA covers agents acting at the order, request or under the direction of a FOREIGN PRINCIPAL. A domestic advocacy organisation - INCLUDING one whose entire subject matter is another country's affairs - registers under the LDA instead and appears nowhere in FARA. AIPAC is the case that proves it: its LDA footprint is 100 filings, one client, and the client is the registrant - in-house lobbying, no outside firm under that name - and it is not a FARA registrant. Whether it ought to be is a live public argument that no database settles, and this desk reports the absence as an absence. THERE IS ALSO NO FARA CONNECTOR IN THIS TOOLKIT AT ALL, so every name here is answered by senatelda, fec, opencorporates and usaspending only; FARA itself is a manual lookup at justice.gov/nsd-fara. The firms listed are SEARCH STRINGS for the LDA, not an assertion about any current foreign client.

real_estate_capital.note: THE CAPITAL BEHIND THE BUILDINGS - AND THE ONE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES EVERY SENTENCE. BLACKROCK AND BLACKSTONE ARE DIFFERENT COMPANIES and conflating them is the most common error in this subject. BlackRock is an ASSET MANAGER: its index funds hold shares as fiduciary for other people's retirement money, so 'BlackRock owns X' almost always means 'funds BlackRock manages hold X on behalf of pension holders' - a different sentence with different consequences, and one that a 13F filing states plainly. Blackstone is a PRIVATE EQUITY and real-estate firm that takes DIRECT ownership, which is the concrete and documentable version. The bridge to the Ohio work is direct: QTS Data Centers is Blackstone-owned and is already in the datacenters set. NOTE WHAT THESE REGISTERS CANNOT SEE: a private REIT's holdings, an LLC's beneficial owner, and any county parcel - the last of which is where a real-estate story actually lives.
